transcript:
Doctor: What brings you in today?
Patient: I've had a fever and a cough with yellow sputum for three days, and I get short of breath climbing stairs.
Doctor: Any chest pain?
Patient: No chest pain.
Doctor: On examination there are crackles at the right base. Temperature 38.4, pulse 102, BP 128/80, SpO2 94%.
Doctor: I think this is community acquired pneumonia. Start amoxicillin 500 mg three times a day for 5 days. We will check a CBC and CRP. Follow up in two days.

Doctor: Your readings at home have been high.
Patient: Yes, around 160 over 100, and I get headaches in the morning.
Doctor: BP today is 162/98. This is essential hypertension. Start amlodipine 5 mg once daily. Let's repeat a creatinine and electrolytes. Review in four weeks.

Patient: I'm passing urine frequently and I'm very thirsty all the time.
Doctor: Your HbA1c came back at 8.2. You have type 2 diabetes. Start metformin 500 mg twice daily with meals. We'll repeat the HbA1c in three months.

Patient: It burns when urinating and I need to go often since yesterday.
Patient: No fever.
Doctor: Abdomen is soft, mild suprapubic tenderness. This looks like a urinary tract infection. Give ciprofloxacin 500 mg BD for 3 days and send a urine culture.

Patient: I've been wheezing at night and my chest feels tight.
Doctor: Known asthma since childhood?
Patient: Yes.
Doctor: Wheeze heard on auscultation, SpO2 96%. This is an asthma exacerbation. Start salbutamol inhaler 0.1 mg as needed and prednisolone 40 mg once daily for 5 days.

Patient: I get a burning feeling behind my breastbone after meals, worse when lying down.
Doctor: Sounds like acid reflux. Diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease. Start pantoprazole 40 mg once daily before breakfast for 4 weeks.

Patient: I feel tired all the time and I've gained weight.
Doctor: Your TSH is raised. You have hypothyroidism. Start levothyroxine 0.05 mg once daily. Recheck TSH in six weeks.

Patient: My heart has been racing on and off for a week.
Doctor: The ECG shows atrial fibrillation. Start metoprolol 25 mg twice daily and warfarin 5 mg once daily. Check INR in 3 days.

Patient: My ankles are swollen and I get breathless lying flat.
Doctor: There is pitting edema noted to the shins and crackles at both bases. This is heart failure. Start furosemide 40 mg once daily. Continue lisinopril. Order an NT-proBNP.

Patient: Sore throat and runny nose for two days, body ache.
Doctor: Throat is mildly red, chest is clear. This is a common cold. Take paracetamol 650 mg every 8 hours as needed. No antibiotics needed.

Patient: I get one-sided headaches with nausea, and light bothers me.
Doctor: Neurological exam is normal. This is migraine. Take ibuprofen 400 mg at onset, up to three times a day.

Patient: Loose motions and vomiting since last night.
Doctor: Mild dehydration, abdomen soft and non tender. Likely gastroenteritis. Start metronidazole 400 mg three times daily for 5 days and oral fluids.

Patient: More breathless than usual and coughing up green sputum.
Doctor: You have known COPD for years. Wheeze heard bilaterally. This is an exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Start azithromycin 500 mg once daily for 3 days and prednisolone 40 mg once daily for 5 days.

Patient: I take ibuprofen most days for my knee.
Doctor: Your eGFR has dropped to 45. This is chronic kidney disease stage 3. Stop ibuprofen. Use paracetamol 500 mg up to four times daily instead. Repeat creatinine in two weeks.

Patient: I've been tired and dizzy for a month.
Doctor: Hemoglobin is 9.1. This is anemia. We'll check a CBC with ferritin. Follow up next week.

Patient: High fever for four days with severe body pain and a rash.
Doctor: Platelets are 90 thousand and NS1 is positive. This is dengue fever. Take paracetamol 500 mg every six hours as needed. Avoid ibuprofen and aspirin. Repeat CBC tomorrow.

Patient: Facial pain and blocked nose for ten days, with headache.
Doctor: Tender over the maxillary sinuses. This is acute sinusitis. Start amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily for 7 days.

Patient: I have diabetes and high blood pressure for years. Today I have a cough and fever.
Doctor: Chest has crackles on the left. I suspect pneumonia. Start azithromycin 500 mg once daily for 3 days. Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily.

Patient: Chest pain after lifting weights yesterday.
Doctor: ECG and troponin are normal, so this is not a heart attack. There is tenderness over the chest wall. Take paracetamol 650 mg three times daily for 3 days.

Nurse: Temperature 39.2, heart rate 124, BP 88/54, respiratory rate 26.
Doctor: She is confused and hypotensive. This is sepsis, likely from a urinary tract infection. Give ceftriaxone 2000 mg once daily. Check lactate and blood cultures now.
